scope: Publication copy of the completed build record; original observations retained under their recorded conditions
retained: checksummed Roundhouse and Spinel patch series and their integrated diffs
final, control, candidate and diagnostic gates, captured app evidence and binary identities
one-patch omission conditions: series, manifests, Dockerfiles, build and gate scripts, apply, probe and recovery results
regression sources, bisect records, reductions, traces and outcomes
retirement checks, pin summaries, upstream links and the candidate-01 and final replays

derived_evidence.method: Each checksummed series replayed with git apply on a clean checkout of its pinned head; the patched tree matches the vendor-tree digest in final-pins.json, and the diff is git diff of that tree. Its numstat equals the run.json delta.

normalization: Host checkout paths are repository-relative; the build record's own location is shown as this record's path, and the v10 build record as the published v10 record.

$SCRATCH stands for the build's local working directory outside the record (emitted programs, native Spinel trees, traces, toolchain contexts and helper scripts); it is not published. $SCRATCH/fresh-build.sh is byte-identical to reproduce/fresh-build.sh.
Upstream author email addresses in the quoted first-bad commit are redacted with the tools/scrub.py email rule; synthetic fixture addresses remain.

Omission folders keep only the files that differ from the final record (series, SHA256SUMS, Dockerfiles, build and gate scripts) plus their apply, probe and recovery results; byte-identical copies are omitted. The candidate-01 omission folders are omitted whole; their execution records and build logs stay in evidence/execution, and invalid-omission-cache.json explains the exclusion. Those records (labels ending -01) name evidence/omissions/without-NN/ paths, where their inputs lived when they ran; the build record later moved them to evidence/omissions-candidate-01/, so the files now at evidence/omissions/ belong to the final omissions (-02).
Captured app logs and binary identities of the compiled gates and the omission gates, and the recovery records, are promoted from generated gate workspaces (promoted_evidence).
The draft upstream issue text and a coordination note between build sessions are omitted: they are messages, not evidence. The issue that was filed is linked from the README.
Retired patches 85, 91 and 92 were byte-identical copies of the v10 record's published patches; the README links the v10 copies.
upstream-links.json keeps each PR's link, title, state, merge time and merge commit; PR bodies are omitted.

run.json describes the input series without internal work-item labels, adds the integrated-diff sources, keeps only the Docker lock, prefix and port constraints, links this inventory and adds an upstream_after_pins note to each new regression. Retirement checks, the patch scoreboard and the excluded-omission record drop internal work-item labels and session wording, and the Spinel classification drops the reference to the unpublished draft issue. Recorded results are unchanged.

The README states peak RSS in KiB from each final compiled gate log (v10 compiled-gate-02, v11 compiled-gate-04). The MiB row in timing-vs-v10.json and run.json mixes sources: its v10 figures are compiled-gate-02 KiB divided by 1,000, its v11 figures build-final-01 KiB divided by 1,024.
The README attributes the without-60 refusal to emission: in that build log roundhouse check exits 0 before roundhouse --target spinel refuses two controllers. The recorded finding text is unchanged.

Upstream status after the pins (matz/spinel#10462 and its fix 3ca03ede9; the keyless-save state of Roundhouse main d8412f3a5 and of #1295's parent 7f20914d5) was checked at publication with native and CRuby probes outside this condition; it is reported as such and changes no recorded result.

The source variant, toolchain Dockerfiles, reproduction scripts and checksummed patches are byte-identical to the supplied record. The variant is byte-identical to the v10 record's, and its ledger, COMPILE-VARIANT.md, is the same file as in the v8, v9 and v10 records.
excluded_results: Intermediate, superseded and cached-build attempts (compiled-gate-02, the candidate-01 omissions) remain diagnostics, not final passing conditions.
